messages.content:
Three independent readers read the same non-disclosure agreement (NDA) and decided whether it supports one statement (the hypothesis). They may agree or disagree, and a program has checked each of their quotes against the document. Your job is to make the final decision yourself, from the document.

<document>
<document 540 omitted, sha256 565c38568fee7085>
</document>

<hypothesis>
Confidential Information shall only include technical information.
</hypothesis>

<readings>
<reading id="A">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 85
reason: The NDA defines confidential Evaluation Material broadly to include business plans, financial condition, customers, operations and more, not only technical information, so the hypothesis that confidential information is limited to technical information is false.
<quote check="exact">the Evaluation Material furnished to it hereunder shall be treated as confidential</quote>
<quote check="exact">which may include information concerning their respective business prospects and plans, financial condition, technology, customers, know-how, trade secrets, operations, assets and liabilities</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="B">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 96
reason: The Evaluation Material (the agreement's term for confidential information) covers business, financial, customer and operational information in addition to technology, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">which may include information concerning their respective business prospects and plans, financial condition, technology, customers, know-how, trade secrets, operations, assets and liabilities</quote>
</reading>
<reading id="C">
label: Contradiction
confidence: 92
reason: The Evaluation Material covers business, financial, customer, and operational information as well as technology, so it is not limited to technical information.
<quote check="exact">which may include information concerning their respective business prospects and plans, financial condition, technology, customers, know-how, trade secrets, operations, assets and liabilities (collectively, the “Evaluation Material”)</quote>
</reading>
</readings>

The readings are evidence about where to look, not votes: a majority can be wrong, and a quote marked "missing" was not found in the document. Read the relevant parts of the document yourself.

Choose exactly one label:
- Entailment: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is true.
- Contradiction: the document states or clearly implies that the hypothesis is false.
- NotMentioned: the document does not address the hypothesis, or says too little to decide.

Evidence is required. For Entailment or Contradiction, give 1 to 3 quotes copied character for character from the document (no paraphrase, no ellipses), each as short as it can be while still carrying the point. They will be checked against the document. For NotMentioned, give an empty list.

Give a confidence from 0 to 100: your probability, in percent, that your label is correct. Give a one-sentence reason.

Answer only with the JSON object the response format asks for: label, confidence, quotes, reason.

content.text: {"label": "Contradiction", "confidence": 93, "quotes": ["which may include information concerning their respective business prospects and plans, financial condition, technology, customers, know-how, trade secrets, operations, assets and liabilities"], "reason": "The Evaluation Material covers business plans, financial condition, customers, operations and other non-technical information, so it is not limited to technical information."}
